the electromagnetic field, as well as other fields, can be described as a superposition of plane waves of a single frequency, the fundamental frequency of the field in question.

the quantum theory is the theory of the equivalence of the space-time and the internal degrees of freedom of elementary particles, and that the quantum field theory is the extension of the relativity theory from space-time to the internal degrees of the freedom of elementary particles.

a tentative program for the extension of the Einstein relativistic theory of space and time to include electromagnetism and other interactions.
a generalization of Einstein's equivalence principle to electromagnetism, and more general interactions, between Fermi- and Bose-fields.
a tentative program of the development of a quantum field theory as a natural extension of the equivalence argument of general relativity.

the principle of equivalence is the key to a unified field theory, which is the only possible way to a general quantum field theory.
